mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses equity discount rates and boosts S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days, as historical data shows positive returns in 65% of such periods.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as consumer spending weakens.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises by >0.5pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales (both above their 3-month moving averages) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are rising above their 3-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), rising inflation erodes real earnings and triggers Fed tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline exceeding 1.0% signals manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as corporate output falls.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO falls by >1.0% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 1.5% annualized indicates strong economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through elevated corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) signal a tightening labor market, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, prompting Fed policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises by >0.3pp in a month.
